Resolved Incident ID: INC-6870
Service: payment-gateway
Title: Flash Sale Spike: Connection Pool Exhaustion & 504 Timeouts
Symptoms: 504 Gateway Timeout on POST /api/v1/charge, active HikariCP pool at 100% capacity (20/20 connections), error rate spiking to 48%.
Root Cause: HikariCP connection pool max size was capped at 20 default connections. Under high concurrent checkout requests, database connections were held during external Stripe API calls without timeouts, starving pool threads.
Runbook Applied: RB-PAY-04: Emergency connection pool scale & socket timeout patch
Resolution Notes: Applied Runbook: RB-PAY-04: Emergency connection pool scale & socket timeout patch

metadata.title: Flash Sale Spike: Connection Pool Exhaustion & 504 Timeouts
metadata.runbook: RB-PAY-04: Emergency connection pool scale & socket timeout patch
metadata.rootCause: HikariCP connection pool max size was capped at 20 default connections. Under high concurrent checkout requests, database connections were held during external Stripe API calls without timeouts, starving pool threads.
resolutionSteps: Bumped HikariCP maximumPoolSize from 20 to 150 via Helm environment config.
Applied 3000ms read timeout on downstream Stripe HTTP client calls to release pooled connections quickly.
Flushed transient deadlock keys in Redis cluster.

Incident ID: INC-2024-8841
Service: payment-gateway
Severity: CRITICAL
Title: HikariCP Connection Pool Exhaustion under Flash Sale Concurrency
Symptoms: 504 Gateway Timeout on POST /api/v1/charge, spikes in active DB pool connection metrics (100% capacity), HTTP 500 error rate > 45%.
Root Cause: HikariCP connection pool max size was capped at 20 default connections. Under high concurrent checkout requests, database connections were held during external Stripe API calls without timeouts, starving pool threads.
Runbook Executed: RB-PAY-04: Emergency connection pool scale & socket timeout patch
Resolution Steps: Bumped HikariCP maximumPoolSize from 20 to 150 via Helm environment config.; Applied 3000ms read timeout on downstream Stripe HTTP client calls to release pooled connections quickly.; Flushed transient deadlock keys in Redis cluster.
Learned Best Practice: Never perform synchronous external HTTP calls while holding an open database transaction lock. Set explicit HTTP client connection & read timeouts.
MTTR: 4 minutes

content:
Incident ID: INC-2024-7302
Service: auth-service
Severity: HIGH
Title: Node.js Heap Memory Leak in RS256 JWT Key Cache
Symptoms: auth-service pod restart loop (OOMKilled exit code 137), RSS memory growing linearly by 85MB/min under high auth token verification volume.
Root Cause: JWKS key cache map in Auth0 verification middleware used un-capped key string keys without TTL eviction, causing heap accumulation on every token refresh.
Runbook Executed: RB-AUTH-09: Hot-reload LRU cache patch & rolling restart
Resolution Steps: Replaced standard JavaScript Object key cache with quick-lru capped at 1000 entries.; Issued rolling restart across auth-service deployment (`kubectl rollout restart deployment/auth-service`).; Increased container memory limits from 512Mi to 1Gi as temporary buffer.
Learned Best Practice: All in-memory caches in microservices MUST have strict size bounds and TTL eviction to prevent RSS memory leak OOMKilled crashes.
MTTR: 6 minutes

content:
Incident ID: INC-2024-6119
Service: redis-cluster
Severity: HIGH
Title: Redis Cache Stampede & Thundering Herd on Product Catalog Key
Symptoms: Database CPU utilization spiked to 99%, microservice latency degraded from 12ms to 4800ms following scheduled cache key expiration.
Root Cause: Hot cache key 'cat:homepage:v2' expired at top of the hour. 5,000 concurrent client threads simultaneously missed cache and hammered primary PostgreSQL DB instance.
Runbook Executed: RB-REDIS-02: Mutex lock caching & probabilistic early expiration
Resolution Steps: Enabled single-flight / mutex lock pattern on catalog service cache miss fallback.; Re-populated hot cache key manually using redis-cli with background worker script.; Implemented randomized jitter (±300s) on key expiration TTLs.
Learned Best Practice: Prevent thundering herd by using single-flight request coalescing for DB queries and applying TTL jitter to popular cache keys.
MTTR: 5 minutes

content:
Incident ID: INC-2024-9104
Service: db-primary
Severity: CRITICAL
Title: Autovacuum Lock Contention & Transaction ID Mappings Spike
Symptoms: PostgreSQL Write-Ahead Logging (WAL) disk space 92% full, transaction ID wraparound warning alerts, blocking locks on user_sessions table.
Root Cause: Long-running analytics query in background reporting worker held open transaction snapshot for over 6 hours, preventing autovacuum from cleaning dead tuples.
Runbook Executed: RB-DB-07: Cancel idle transactions & trigger targeted vacuum analyze
Resolution Steps: Terminated blocking analytics query PID using `SELECT pg_cancel_backend(pid)`.; Ran manual `VACUUM ANALYZE VERBOSE user_sessions;`.; Configured `statement_timeout = 30s` on default analytics reporting role.
Learned Best Practice: Always enforce statement_timeout on non-OLTP analytical database connections to prevent autovacuum freeze and transaction ID wraparound.
MTTR: 8 minutes

content:
Incident ID: INC-2024-5512
Service: payment-gateway
Severity: MEDIUM
Title: Stripe Webhook Signature Verification Failures due to Proxy Header Truncation
Symptoms: Payment status stuck in 'PENDING', 400 Bad Request responses on incoming webhook notifications from Stripe endpoint.
Root Cause: NGINX ingress controller header buffer size (4k) truncated long `Stripe-Signature` headers during TLS cipher renegotiation.
Runbook Executed: RB-PAY-12: Ingress buffer size override & webhook retry trigger
Resolution Steps: Updated NGINX ingress annotation: `nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/proxy-buffer-size: '16k'`.; Triggered Stripe API event resend CLI command to replay missed webhook payloads.
Learned Best Practice: Configure ingress proxy buffer sizes to at least 16k when receiving cryptographically signed webhook headers from third-party APIs.
MTTR: 3 minutes
